worked_solution:
If we let $u=-x$, then 

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-1\,⟹\,-\text{d}u=\text{d}x.
$$

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {5}^{-x}\,\text{d}x & =\int {5}^{u}\cdot (-1)\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\int {5}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{{5}^{u}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}+C \\  & =-\frac{{5}^{-x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}+C\end{aligned}
$$
